plan: Hold the workspace as a single deep-copied dict tree; deep-copy again in to_data() so internal state is never aliased.
Compute total_word_count with a recursive fold: notes count \b\w+\b runs after replacing [[?id]] markers with a space, references contribute their declared word_count, containers sum children.
Collect unresolved markers into a set from note-text marker identifiers and reference 'unresolved' lists, returning them sorted lexicographically.
Render the outline as the workspace title followed by a depth-first walk emitting two spaces per nesting level plus 'kind: title', with top-level items at depth 1.

Implement move as validate-then-mutate: locate the item and its parent list, resolve the destination (literal 'workspace' or a section/group), reject self/descendant destinations, non-containers, missing or non-string ids, and out-of-range indices — all before any mutation — then pop and append/insert the same dict so failures leave to_data() unchanged and successes preserve the subtree.
Write in-memory unit-style construction only; the module uses just copy and re from the standard library.
mechanisms: Deep-copy isolation at construction and export (copy.deepcopy)
Recursive kind-dispatched fold for word counts (marker-stripped note text, declared reference counts)
Set-union marker collection with sorted output
Depth-first outline emitter with two-space-per-level indentation
Parent-list finder returning (list, index, item) for in-place list surgery
Validate-then-mutate move guaranteeing atomicity on failure
Subtree-containment check to forbid moving a container into itself or its descendants
